Ib. 27ᵃ אמר ק׳ וכ׳ the text reads babboḳer &c.

<cite ref="Berakhot 29b:9">Ib. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי קראה</he> where is the Biblical passage to prove it? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 45b:8">Snh. 45ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 71a:13">71ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>בעינן ק׳ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="K01340"><he>כְּתַב</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Keritot 11b:77">Ker. 11ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ק׳ בעי</he> do we need a Bible verse for it?; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Berakhot 30b:2">Ber. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>פוק קרא קְרָאָיךְ לברא</he> go out, read thy verse in the street, i.e. thy authority is not recognized at college; <cite ref="Ketubot 56a">Keth. 56ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yevamot 40a:24">Yeb. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>קַרְיָיךְ</he>, v. <cite ref="S02051"><he>קַרְיָיא</he></cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="S01882"><he>קְרָאֵי</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 3b:13">M. Kat. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>והני … ק׳ נינהו</he> are these traditional rulings? are they not intimated in the Biblical text? <cite ref="Pesachim 4b:9">Pes. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>תרי ק׳ כתיבי</he> there are two verses (seemingly contradictory); a. v. fr.
